title: Who Can Top the Board With a Bonus
statement:
A leaderboard has scores, where scores[i] is player i's points. You have one bonus of extra points to hand to a single player.

For every player, decide: if that player alone got the whole bonus, would they have the highest score on the board? A tie for first place counts as having the highest score.

Return a list of booleans, one per player, in the same order as scores.

examples.why: The top score is 9. Player 2 reaches 6 + 3 = 9 and ties it, which counts. Player 0 reaches only 7.
With no bonus, everyone is already tied for first.
Compare with the original top score of 10, not with the top after someone else gets a bonus: 1 + 8 = 9 still falls short.

hints: What is the one number every player has to reach?
The bonus goes to one player only, so everyone else keeps their original score. The target is the original maximum.
Find the maximum once, then compare scores[i] + bonus with it for each i.

explain.intuition:
Only one player gets the bonus at a time, so the rest of the board does not move. The bar to clear is always the same: the current top score. A player qualifies when scores[i] + bonus ≥ max.

The slow way rescans the board for each player. Finding the maximum once first turns it into two simple passes.
steps: Scan scores once to find top, the largest value.
For each player, push scores[i] + bonus >= top.
pitfalls: Using > instead of >=. A tie for first counts.
Rebuilding the maximum for each player, including other players' imaginary bonuses.

solutions.title: Rescan for each player
solutions.idea: For each player, check every other score against scores[i] + bonus.

solutions.title: Compare with the maximum
solutions.idea: The bar is the original top score. Find it once, then compare each player with it.

followups: The bonus may be split between any players. What is the largest number of players who can all tie for first at once?
Scores update live. How do you answer each query in O(1) while keeping the maximum current?
lcTitle: Kids With the Greatest Number of Candies
